summary: Remote-controlled shell/PTY daemon connecting to a WebSocket gateway
details: The package installs a `whalent` daemon binary that opens a WebSocket connection to a remote gateway (default `wss://memory.whalent.com`, overridable via `--gateway`) and executes commands received from that gateway on the local host. The bundled runtime (dist/core.cjs) combines a WebSocket client with `node-pty` and `child_process.spawn` driven by `process.env.SHELL`, plus references to loopback RDP/VNC ports (127.0.0.1:3389, 5900, 5901), consistent with the remote party driving shell/PTY sessions and remote-desktop tunnels on the operator's machine. The README states the daemon 'accepts remote commands (upgrade, restart) via the gateway,' but the full command surface is not visible: both dist/index.cjs (~114 KB) and dist/core.cjs (~13.6 MB) are shipped as javascript-obfuscator output (string-array rotation, control-flow flattening, hex-mangled identifiers), so the actual set of verbs the gateway can invoke on the host cannot be enumerated from the tarball. Whoever controls the gateway domain has full-host code execution on any machine running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
